In case you’re wondering, the card is being distributed as part of the Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration, which commemorates three decades of the card game. The Pokémon 30th Anniversary expansion, as a whole, launched its first wave on September 16 and includes a mix of new artwork, returning cards, and a set of 30 unique Pikachu rare cards. You’ll find one card featuring Pikachu in every booster pack.

The Mewtwo promo itself has a design that separates it from a regular card pulled from the 30th Celebration expansion. It features Mewtwo alongside Pokémon’s 30th-anniversary branding and the “What’s Your Favorite?” logo. Buyers also receive a separate card containing a QR code that directs them to learn more about the Pokémon Night Out experience, an EDM x Pokémon concert experience planned as part of the anniversary celebrations.
How Mewtwo Is Perfect For Pokémon 30th Anniversary Celebrations

Mewtwo also feels like a fitting Pokémon to receive an anniversary promo, considering how closely the character is tied to the franchise’s early years. It was one of the most memorable Pokémon from the original 151 and played a major role in the first Pokémon movie, making it a familiar face even to fans who have been away from the TCG for years. The character has also remained a regular presence in Pokémon merchandise, games, and special card releases. For collectors, that makes this particular promo more interesting than a random anniversary card, especially with the 30th-anniversary branding attached to it.

GameStop has been used for similar Pokémon TCG promotions before, including retailer-exclusive stamped cards. This time, however, the card won’t carry a GameStop logo. Instead, the Mewtwo card uses the anniversary branding, which gives the same promo a consistent look across the participating retailers.

In case you’re planning to slack off, it’s best to avoid treating October 2 as just another release date. As per the official announcement, you can only get the Mewtwo Pokémon TCG card while supplies last at the retailer you’re planning to visit. Spending $15 doesn’t necessarily lock in a card for you, so I recommend heading to the retailer or hopping on its online storefront soon after the promo goes live.
